title: Load custom resource with PackedFloat32Array deserializes incorrect size if default is declared
body: ### Tested versions Found using 4.6.0 official build Also tested and reproduced in: Godot 4.6.1 Godot 4.5.1 Godot 4.4.1 ### System information Godot v4.6.1.stable - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - dedicated AMD Radeon RX 9060 XT (Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.; 32.0.23027.2005) - AMD Ryzen 5 7600 6-Core Processor (12 threads) - 31.60 GiB memory ### Issue description A resource using PackedFloat32Array that has a default value in its declaration deserializes as a array of length 24 regardless of what was saved. The saved resource file does however contain all original data. ### Steps to reproduce A m.r.p. is included below. 1. Open the MRP project 2. Issue is tested by `@tool` script on open 3. See output of test result in console 4. Test code in issue_reproduce.gd MRP tests 2 cases using 2 variants of basically the same resource: one with and one without a default empty array declaration. - In both cases, before saving, the default is replaced in code with a new array - Case with a default empty array value fails, it loads back with a size of 24 (this seems constant, regardless of the amount saved) and causes the fail report and assert. - Using .res or .tres, compressed or uncompressed, all makes no difference in outcome of both tests. Disabling test B (which passes), and inspecting the .tres saved by test A (which fails); it can be observed the data is saved in the file: However, opening the .tres in godot, reveals the **inspector says '0'**: _(opposed to the **'24' by code** when loading)_ TL;DR without having to open the MRP: _Resource extending class with:_ ```gdscript @export var float32_array: PackedFloat32Array = [] -> with 600 elements, reads back as 24 elements @export var float32_array: PackedFloat32Array -> with 600 elements, reads back as 600 elements ``` ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [MRP-float-buffer-resource-issue.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25648123/MRP-float-buffer-resource-issue.zip)
